meta.applies_to: CS2 Transfer Line 3.0, DES v10.0 (unchanged code) + DV10 timing/auxiliary power (= 'DES v10.1' behaviour, implemented in cs2_mdo/udes_2_0), MDA 1.5, disruption scenario set CS2-DS-v2 (DS0-DS15) of UDES 1.1
modelling_decisions: objectives for UMDO 2.0: max E[TH_d] (mean throughput under disruption), min E[E_d], max E[R_phi(t_f)]; R_rate, TTR, RL, PL, TST, TUT and TH_d are reported only
restoration-time coefficients: product over all DVs, level 1 = base for every DV (no normalisation to a reference design); mean and standard deviation scaled
DV10 throughput/energy: use the table values; generic mechanism chosen by the modeller (uniform timing factor + constant auxiliary power)
adaptation mechanisms: manual fallback, ramp-up after restart, backlog catch-up by a temporary speed-up at extra energy
R_phi evaluated at t_f = restoration + 60 min
meta.status: engineering assumptions (switch-over delay, manual-time factor, ramp start/duration, speed-up and energy exponent) of the uncertainty model; not measured

restoration_time.distribution: truncated_normal (lower bound 0), parameters of the underlying normal (as UDES 1.1)
restoration_time.note: All other DV levels have coefficient 1.0 for all four variables (spreadsheet columns J-M).

reference.design: TL3 DES baseline (DV1 = 1 shuttle, other DVs at their baseline levels), 8 h

dv10.mechanism: timing factor s = throughput coefficient: every DES duration (operations, manual tasks, corrections, wake-ups, repositioning, shuttle travel, station-release clearance) is divided by s, so the periodic cycle rate of every design scales by exactly s; a constant auxiliary power P_aux (maintenance / condition-monitoring equipment, always on) is calibrated so that the baseline 8-h energy equals the energy coefficient x 5560.895 Wh. Restoration durations, the fallback switch-over and the ramp durations are NOT scaled (real time).

calibration.basis: TL3 baseline Z131331321x, 1 shuttle, 8 h, nominal (DS0)
calibration.note: TH_ss_DES is the periodic cycle rate (continuous); TH_8h_DES = completed products / 8 h is quantised by batches of 9 products, so it can differ from the target by up to one batch.

manual_fallback.operator: one dedicated fallback operator (capacity 1, 0 W); collaborative tasks (station operator already present) use their station operator
manual_fallback.note: Manual time = calibrated level-1 manual task time (alternatives_calibration.json) x manual_time_factor / s(DV10). The two UR10 transfer tasks without a manual DV alternative use the manual/automated ratio of the WS6 tray loading. Workstation equipment of the manual alternative draws its calibrated active power during fallback work. Robot repositioning and wake-ups are skipped while the robot is down and its task is done manually. A task started manually is finished manually even if the robot is restored meanwhile. No fallback for a failed shuttle (lifting it off the track is not modelled).

ramp_up.note: After restoration the resource works at c(t) = c0 + (1 - c0) S((t - t_rest)/T), S(x) = 3x^2 - 2x^3, T = max(300 s, 0.2 x outage) (same shape and duration rule as case study 1). Energy: constant active power during slowed work (longer wall time).

catch_up.eligible: segments whose resources are all machines (robots, FANUC cell/conveyor, UR3e_WS9) and shuttle travel; tasks with a human are not sped up
catch_up.activation: from every breakdown until production is back on plan: with no resource down, N_disrupted(t) >= N_nominal(t) of the same design (latched off until the next breakdown)
catch_up.demand: the design's own nominal plan (DS0 cumulative production); no overtime (8-h shift)
catch_up.note: Active power x speed_factor^energy_exponent while sped up (+32 %); the DES energy table charges active_W over the shorter wall time, the remainder is added as catch-up energy.

termination_options.count: UMDA 2.0 rule: catch-up ends at the first decision point with no resource down and N_dis(t) >= N_nom(t); can leave a phase lag of up to one batch
termination_options.time_lag: catch-up ends at the first decision point with no resource down and the latest disrupted batch completed no later than the nominal plan reached the same cumulative count (time lag <= 0)

R_phi.performance: phi(t) = cumulative production relative to the nominal plan; backlog B(t) = N_nom(t) - N_dis(t), both linearly interpolated between batch completions
R_phi.formula: episode: R = 1 - [B(t_f) - B(t_e)] / L, L = max_{t in [t_e, t_f]} B(t) - B(t_e), clipped to [0, 1]; scenario: sum(L - D) / sum(L) over episodes (D = clipped B(t_f) - B(t_e)); R = 1 if sum(L) < L_min
R_phi.episode_end: t_f = min(t_restored + offset, next failure time, 8 h)

resilience.reporting_metrics_convention: UMDA 1.1 principal convention: W = 30 min trailing window, tau = 40 min, steady reference, event approach (cs2_mdo/umda11/metrics.py, unchanged)

acceptance.physical_consistency: R_phi decreases with the restoration duration (within design and scenario) and increases with the strategies (with vs without)
